stem: Which of the following is the most correct regarding diagnosis of viral infections?

options.text: Viral culture is the best test because it is sensitive and specific and allows for rapid identification of the virus
Viral serology testing is quick and easy to perform and should be the first test for any viral infection
PCR testing is very useful for diagnosis of viral infections but it does not allow for identification of antiviral resistance
PCR testing is highly sensitive and specific and allows for rapid identification of most pathogenic viruses

explanation: PCR-based nucleic acid testing is generally the preferred diagnostic approach for many viral infections because it is rapid, highly sensitive, and highly specific. Viral culture is slower and less commonly used, serology is often retrospective rather than first-line, and PCR may also detect some resistance mutations depending on the assay and virus.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect: viral culture is slow and not the best rapid diagnostic test for most viruses.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect: serology is not usually the first-line test for acute viral diagnosis.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect: while not all PCR assays assess resistance, some molecular tests can identify antiviral resistance mutations.
optionExplanations.D: Correct: PCR is rapid and highly sensitive/specific for many viral pathogens.
